one_month_reasoning: The scheduled event in the window is Q3 2026 earnings, estimated for Thu 2026-10-22 after the close but not yet confirmed by Intel (no 8-K; supervisor check), so the 10-31 close very likely includes the reaction. Guidance was $15.8-16.8B revenue, $0.38 non-GAAP EPS, ~42% gross margin (source #1). A beat is likely given seven straight beats and supply-constrained server CPUs (source #6, source #20, source #21), but the stock is ~58x FY27 EPS after a +258% year and the supervisor recomputed that 8 of the last 11 next-day reactions were negative with a mean absolute move of ~11%. New for round 2: Intel's own lock-up ends at the earlier of 90 days or the Q3 release (424B5, source #2) and the shelf stays open, so a raise right after the print is possible though nothing is announced; with $50.5B debt and 2027 capex guided higher, that is a small extra left-tail weight. I keep a near-symmetric distribution with median about $118.5 (slight downside tilt for the negative reaction base rate, rates and the lock-up expiry) and a 1-month sigma of ~21% with a fatter-tailed 20% component (sigma ~32%) for the earnings gap.

fair_value.method: Blend of P/E ($2.55 NTM EPS a year out x 35x = $89), SOTP ($100) and EV/sales (7x $72B 2027 revenue = $91), weighted 0.40/0.35/0.25 = ~$94, on 5.45B shares (greenshoe and partial escrow included), ~$2B pro forma net debt and $15.6B NCI.

methods.name: P/E
methods.inputs: NTM EPS at Oct-2027 $2.55 (on 5.45B shares) x 35x

inputs_detail.input: NTM EPS as of Oct-2027 (Q4'27 + 3/4 of 2028)
inputs_detail.derivation: Consensus 2027 EPS $2.06 (source #6, source #21) and normalized 2028 ~ $3 (source #3) blend to ~$2.75. Round 1 cut 10% partly on Northland's May call for a CY27 datacenter decline (source #8); since then FY27 consensus rose ~35% in 90 days (supervisor), so I halve that haircut to ~5% ($2.60), then take ~2% off for the 242.1M offering shares incl. the greenshoe (source #25) and partial escrow release not fully in consensus share counts: $2.55.

Unchanged: AMD ~40x forward, NVDA ~25x (source #6); Northland called 38x on $3.20 expensive (source #8); Intel 5-yr median ~12x (source #13). 35x prices growth and a foundry option without a shortage-peak multiple.

methods.name: SOTP
methods.inputs: Products ~$22B 2027 op income, after 15% tax $18.7B x 25x = $467B; Foundry $125B; Mobileye/Altera stakes $9.4B; minus unallocated corporate costs $40B, net debt $2B and NCI $15.6B = ~$544B / 5.45B shares = ~$100.

inputs_detail.derivation: About 14% growth on the Q2 run-rate, in line with consensus 2027 revenue growth of ~14% (source #21).
Same multiple source #5 uses for Intel Products, inside the 25-40x range of semi peers (source #6).

About 1.2x net PP&E of $105.7B (source #1). Foundry still loses ~$2.1-2.5B a quarter on $293M of external revenue (source #1, source #5) with breakeven at risk of slipping to 2028 (source #3). Raised $5B from round 1 because the CEO kept 14A on track for H2'27 risk production and 2028 HVM on the Q2 call (source #28) and Tesla has selected 14A for Terafab (source #29), which lowers the chance of a 14A pause; volumes and terms are undisclosed, so I stay far below source #5's ~$250B implied residual. The 80% 18A yield (source #17) is relayed and given no weight.

The SOTP starts from segment operating income, which excludes corporate unallocated costs, so a deduction is needed and does not double-count non-GAAP EPS (the P/E method does not take it). Q2 corporate unallocated was -$1.42B (source #1), much of it amortization, restructuring and SBC; I take ~$2.6B/yr of recurring cost (SBC kept as a real cost, restructuring assumed to fade) after 15% tax x ~18x = ~$40B, trimmed from round 1's $50B.

inputs_detail.input: Net debt (pro forma, after H2 burn)
inputs_detail.derivation: Q2 debt $50.5B less cash $12.9B and ST investments $16.9B (source #1) = $20.7B; less $22.62B net offering proceeds with the greenshoe (source #26, source #25) = ~$1.9B net cash; add ~$4B for H2 cash burn (Q2 adj. FCF -$8.4B, source #1) = ~$2B net debt.

5,285M basic after the full greenshoe (424B5 source #2; 8-K source #25) + ~119M unvested RSUs/PSUs = ~5.40B diluted (supervisor, from the 424B5), plus about half of the 143M escrowed DoC shares that are released as Secure Enclave disbursements arrive within 12 months. The 241M contingent warrants are excluded.

methods.name: EV/sales
methods.inputs: 2027 revenue $72B x 7.0x = $504B EV; less net debt $2B and NCI $15.6B, plus stakes $9.4B = ~$496B / 5.45B = ~$91.

inputs_detail.derivation: source #4 puts the current multiple at about 10x sales, the $74 bear case at 5.9x and the $172 bull at 13.7x. I use 7x, leaning to the bear side because negative FCF and an unproven foundry argue against a full AI-semi multiple.

5,285M basic after the full greenshoe (424B5 source #2; 8-K source #25) + ~119M unvested RSUs/PSUs = ~5.40B diluted (supervisor, from the 424B5), plus about half of the 143M escrowed DoC shares that are released as Secure Enclave disbursements arrive within 12 months. The 241M contingent warrants are excluded.

bear.story: The CPU shortage eases and hyperscaler capex flattens in 2027 (Northland's May call, source #8, now somewhat stale against rising estimates), DCAI growth slows from +59% and server price increases reverse. Tesla's 14A selection (source #29) stays small or slips and no volume Apple commitment follows; foundry breakeven slips to 2028 (source #3) while FCF stays negative and Intel taps the shelf again after the lock-up ends at the Q3 print (source #2). The multiple falls to ~6x sales and ~25x EPS (source #4, source #7). Price $60-75.

base.story: The turnaround continues: DCAI keeps growing, gross margin edges toward the mid-40s, 2027 EPS lands near $2.0-2.2 (source #21), 14A risk production starts on schedule in H2 2027 (source #28) and Tesla/Apple work progresses without disclosed volumes. EPS growth absorbs de-rating from ~58x FY27 toward ~45x NTM; the stock ends a little below spot, near the ~$116 street mean target (source #6).

bull.story: Tesla's Terafab 14A commitment gets volume and terms (source #29), Apple confirms 18A-P (source #19), the agentic-AI CPU shortage persists into 2027 (source #20), credit improves (a Fitch outlook move to stable is reported, source #27) and 2028 EPS heads to $3+ (source #3, source #8). Matches source #4's $172 bull case at ~13.7x sales.

thesis_break_reason: Below about $70 (~6x sales, ~42% below spot; source #4's bear case is $74, source #5's $70) the market would be pricing a fundamental break rather than de-rating: the server-CPU upcycle rolling over and/or 14A losing Tesla and other external interest, with foundry losses at $2B+ a quarter and no breakeven path (source #3, source #6). It is ~26% below the $95 August offering price ($23B gross incl. greenshoe, source #25) and the CEO's $95 purchase (source #16), and well under the July 2026 low of ~$82 that ordinary de-rating reached. A fall to the $80s-90s would be ordinary volatility at 76% realized vol.

reasoning: Skeptic lane, round 2. Facts from round 1 stand: Q2'26 revenue $16.1B (+25%), non-GAAP EPS $0.42, GAAP EPS -$2.16 (escrow mark-to-market), adjusted FCF -$8.4B, debt $50.5B, foundry -$2.1B on $293M external revenue (source #1, source #5). Supervisor corrections I accept and verified: the August raise was $23B gross / $22.62B net with the 31.6M-share greenshoe exercised 2026-08-11 (source #25, source #26), giving 5,285M basic and ~5.40B diluted shares; I use 5.45B to include part of the 143M escrow shares. Net debt falls to ~$2B pro forma after H2 burn; NCI $15.6B still deducted. 14A remains on track for H2'27 risk production and 2028 HVM (source #28), and I note Tesla selected 14A for Terafab in April (source #29), which lowers my 14A-pause odds though volumes and terms are undisclosed. On my own lane: insider selling is small (an EVP's 21k-share and 14.7k-share sales, source #30, source #31) against the CEO's $10M buy at $95 (source #16); my 2025 rating sources are dated, and an X post reports Fitch moved its outlook to Stable after the raise (source #27), which I could not verify at Fitch, so it moves no number, but it weakens the credit-stress leg of the bear case. Northland's CY27 datacenter decline (source #8) is stale against a ~35% rise in FY27 estimates, so I halved the EPS haircut built on it. The capitalized corporate-cost deduction is kept in the SOTP only (segment income excludes those costs, so no double count with non-GAAP EPS) and trimmed to $40B. Net: fair value ~$94 (from $93), since the extra shares offset the higher proceeds, EPS and foundry value. The valuation case is unchanged: ~58x FY27 EPS, ~10x sales, a Hold-heavy street with a ~$116 mean target below spot (source #6). For the ladder I keep a median below spot but raise it to ~$111 (from ~$109), as a compromise between fair value and momentum/rising estimates, with a lognormal sigma ~0.60 plus a 15% wide (sigma 1.0) component for binary foundry/customer news. Scenarios: bear 27% at $65, base 47% at $112, bull 26% at $175 (mean ~$116). P(>=120) ~0.45, P(<72) ~0.25. I disagree with nothing material in the supervisor file; I add the Tesla 14A selection as a fact its key drivers omit. Limits: Fitch and technology.org pages were not reachable (402/403); I used about 10 searches/fetches this round.
